summary: Full end-to-end test of NRSQ + RSQ workflows on Lead Detail page. Backend (4/4) + Frontend (11/11) core assertions PASS. Ops user can generate NRSQ instant quote via top-bar or choice-card, both persist quote_type='nrsq', package_selected, selling_amount, quote_sent_to_customer=true, and flip lead_status to 'Quote Sent to Customer'. RSQ button opens Supplier Mail composer and automatically PATCHes quote_type='rsq' before composer renders — verified persisted after reload (top-bar shifts from nrsq-btn/rsq-btn → send-mail-btn). All regression flows (Trip details, Pipeline lead-status dropdown, Reassign dialog, WhatsApp/Call/SMS quick actions, Contact Timeline) still render correctly. integration_issues.issue: Inconsistent role-gating on LeadDetail.jsx line 70: `canOps = user.role === 'operations' || user.role === 'admin'` hides top-bar nrsq-btn/rsq-btn/nrsq-edit-btn/send-mail-btn for sales users, BUT the mid-page choice-card CTAs (nrsq-cta/rsq-cta) and the inline nrsq-edit button inside nrsq-summary are NOT gated — sales users see and successfully use them. Backend allow-list (server.py line 597-598) explicitly permits sales to update quote_type/package_selected/selling_amount/quote_sent_to_customer/quote_sent_date. The review request explicitly hints 'canOps in the frontend actually covers sales + ops + admin roles' — but the current implementation does NOT include sales. Either (a) include 'sales' in canOps (rename to canQuote), or (b) also gate the choice-card CTAs and inline edit under the same role check to make the UX consistent.

critical_code_review_comments: LeadDetail.jsx line 70 `canOps` is misnamed if it truly should cover 'sales + ops + admin' (per review-request hint). Suggest renaming to `canQuote` and expanding to `['sales','operations','admin']`, then applying the same guard to nrsq-cta / rsq-cta / nrsq-edit inline button inside nrsq-summary — currently they are unguarded, creating a permissioning inconsistency (visible in the UI but implied not by role check).

LeadDetail.jsx line 82-84 openMail() silently swallows PATCH errors with an empty catch — if quote_type update fails (e.g., 403 for a hypothetical read-only role), the mail dialog will still open and the tracker won't render on reload. Consider surfacing a toast on failure.

server.py line 597-598 sales allow-list includes `quote_sent_to_customer` and `quote_sent_date` but NOT `supplier_quote_amount` — that's intentional (Supplier ₹ is ops-only in Quote & Pricing card, matching the disabled={!canOps} on line 326). Good separation.
Radix Dialog warning about missing Description — add <DialogDescription> or aria-describedby={undefined} to nrsq-dialog / reassign-dialog / mail-dialog / ai-dialog for a11y compliance.
action_items: Decide sales-role quote generation policy: EITHER expand canOps to include 'sales' (also update choice-card + inline nrsq-edit gating for consistency) OR remove choice-card + inline nrsq-edit for sales role. Backend already allows sales — current mix creates unclear UX and hides shortcuts sales users could otherwise use.
(Minor) Add <DialogDescription> or aria-describedby to Dialog components to silence Radix a11y warnings on nrsq-dialog/reassign-dialog/mail-dialog/ai-dialog.

rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. UX inconsistency root cause: LeadDetail.jsx introduced two independent render surfaces for NRSQ/RSQ (top-bar + mid-page choice-card) but only the top-bar surface received the canOps role guard. The mid-page card and inline nrsq-edit were left unguarded, so sales users bypass the intended (or unintended) restriction. Backend was updated in a prior iteration to explicitly allow sales to write these fields, suggesting the intended design was to unify roles — the frontend just needs canOps expanded to 'sales' or a new canQuote flag introduced.
